correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the independent exponential CTMC first-step system on states 11,10,01; solved it to \(T=N/D\) with \(D=r(c+r+s)^2+p(s+2c+r)>0\). Two quotient-rule derivatives yield the exact formal factorization of T_xy into a negative positive-denominator prefactor times polynomial P. In the complete positive domain all \(r\)-polynomial coefficients except possibly the constant are strictly positive, so \(P\) strictly increases from \(p(p-cs-2c^2)\) to positive infinity; all threshold and equality regimes follow. Packaged exact integer-coefficient checker proves the derivative identity by zero-polynomial expansion, and exact Fraction first-step checks and an explicit sign-changing finite difference independently corroborate premises. Finite tests are not substituted for the universal proof. Model assumptions and no global finite-increment claim explicitly stated.

originality.rationale: The precise asserted theorem is not stochastic occupancy modeling itself or a first-step extinction-time formula; it is a complete positive-parameter classification of the cross-effect of two local protection actions, including a sharp unique regional-catastrophe crossover. Accessible primary literature covers stochastic occupancy conservation, simulated reserve allocation, correlated disturbances, and uniform management interventions without establishing the specific cross-rate sign law in inspected material. Actual semantic and alias searches of public mathematical result records returned no equivalent theorem. Closely relevant historical papers were not fully accessible; their potential coverage is a substantive residual publication risk, and novelty is not certified solely by searches.

value.rationale: The natural two-reserve conservation question asks if protecting both patches yields more or less joint persistence benefit than adding the separate benefits. Correlated catastrophic risk changes the answer even with fixed local extinction and rescue rates. The theorem proves a nontrivial complete parameter boundary and uniqueness of the regime switch by an exact positive-coefficient quartic, rather than an arbitrary parameter witness or a routine numerical fit. It offers interpretable policy sensitivity without overstating ecological applicability; no general or empirical downstream theorem is claimed.
